overviewPage.anAgentReadsHostsOver: An agent reads hosts over SSH, and Infrastructure reads clusters through their API. Nothing is installed on them.
overviewPage.addAnAgentAndStart: Add an agent and start it, prepare a host with the commands under Setup, add the host, check its key, and the first collection follows within a minute.

setupPage.whatToPutOnHosts: What to put on hosts and clusters so they can be read. Nothing is installed on them.
setupPage.hostsTrustTheCertificateAuthority: Hosts trust the certificate authority of the agent that reads them. Add one under
setupPage.andStartItItsSetup: and start it; its setup shows here.
setupPage.n1TrustTheAgentFor: 1. Trust the agent for one account
setupPage.runAsRootOnThe: Run as root on the host. It creates the openasy account and trusts the CA of {{name}} for that account only, so the CA can never log in as root or anyone else.
setupPage.theAgentAsksTheHost: The agent asks the host for its key; check the fingerprint on the host before accepting it.
setupPage.itStaysOnTheAgent: It stays on the agent, not in Infrastructure. Certificates last 5 minutes and allow no TTY and no forwarding. Fingerprint {{caFingerprint}}.
setupPage.toReachHostsInAnother: To reach hosts in another network through one of them, add it as a host and set AllowTcpForwarding yes for the openasy account on it only. Or run another agent in that network.
setupPage.forHostsWhereSshdConfig: For hosts where sshd_config cannot change. The key cannot open a TTY or forward anything. Prefer certificates: a key lasts until it is removed.
setupPage.kubectlApplyFThisFile: kubectl apply -f this file, then add the cluster with its API server URL, CA and the token from the openasy-infra-token Secret. It cannot read Secrets or ConfigMaps or change anything.
setupPage.theCommandsAboveIncludeA: The commands above include a sudoers file that allows only fixed, read-only commands: which process listens on a port, SSH keys that may log in, sudo rules, the SSH server settings and the firewall rules.
